video.description:
A Use Case Diagram visually represents the relationship between actors and key actions within a business solution. In this video, we'll look at how to draw a use case diagram for business analysts. 
We'll also look at the key components of the model including actors, scenarios, system boundaries, extend and include relationships, as well as generalizations. A use case is a functionality in a system that will allow the user to achieve a goal. It also depicts the scope of that solution.

video.description:
What is Spec-Driven Development and how does it improve AI coding for larger projects?
Spec-Driven Development is an emerging AI coding workflow where AI agents generate code based on structured specifications instead of simple prompts. As AI tools like GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT become common in software development, developers need better ways to manage large AI-generated codebases.

video.description:
Try EdrawMax: https://event.wondershare.com/api/s/3aR

Learn how to create a UML use case diagram in EdrawMax with this step-by-step tutorial.

This video explains use case diagram definition, common symbols, actors, system boundaries, and relationships so you can model user interactions more clearly.

This tutorial is useful for software engineering students, analysts, UML beginners, and developers.

What you'll learn:
- what a UML use case diagram is
- common use case symbols and notation
- how actors and system boundaries work
- how to draw a use case diagram in EdrawMax

FAQ
What is a UML use case diagram?
A UML use case diagram shows how users or external actors interact with a system.
